Why Every Listener try/catches →

A Notification Row per Event

notifyInApp.listener.js: one domainEvents.on() block per event, each writing whichever Notification rows that event implies.

// Figure 5.8: two Notification rows from one ticket.created event (src/events/listeners/notifyInApp.listener.js, excerpt)
domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, async (ticket) => {
  const agents = await prisma.user.findMany({
    where: { role: 'agent' },
    select: { id: true },
  });

  await prisma.notification.createMany({
    data: [
      { userId: ticket.customerId, type: EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, message: `Your ticket "${ticket.subject}" was created.` },
      ...agents.map((agent) => ({ userId: agent.id, type: EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, message: `New ticket in the queue: "${ticket.subject}".` })),
    ],
  });
});

This is exactly the shape the last two topics were building toward: domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, ...) runs whenever anything emits that event — this listener has no idea it's ticket.service.js calling createTicket, and doesn't need to. ticket.created fans out to two recipients here — a confirmation row for the customer, plus one per agent so the queue notification reaches everyone who might pick it up — all in a single createMany rather than one create call per row.

The file has one more domainEvents.on(...) block per remaining event — ticket.assigned writes one row for the newly assigned agent, ticket.commented loops over the recipients the previous topic already resolved, and ticket.status_changed writes one row for the customer using the previousStatus argument updateTicket passed alongside the ticket. Same pattern, four times, each block reacting to exactly one event.
